proposals.label: Military AI challenging arms control
proposals.definition: AI in the military domain and autonomous weapons presented as new challenges for arms control and international regulation.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages explicitly naming military AI or autonomous weapons as arms-control or security challenges.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages where AI is only named in a list of rivalries without military specification (AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION).
proposals.boundary_cases: 'Rivalry in artificial intelligence' as part of an arms race narrative is borderline; code here only if military use is explicit.

examples.quote: the proliferation of advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence in the military domain and autonomous weapons systems, has introduced new challenges for arms control and international regulations

proposals.label: AI listed among global threats
proposals.definition: AI is named briefly within a list of security threats, rivalries or drivers of global crisis, without elaboration.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages where AI appears as one item in a catalogue of threats, crises or rivalries.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude neutral or positive technology lists (AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION) and passages with substantive AI discussion.
proposals.boundary_cases: A list item with an evaluative adjective (e.g. 'uncontrollable') remains a list mention unless the speaker develops the point.

examples.quote: an intense rivalry in space, cybertechnology and artificial intelligence
the seemingly uncontrollable chariots of artificial intelligence

proposals.label: AI as arena of strategic rivalry
proposals.definition: AI framed as a domain of geopolitical rivalry contributing to erosion of trust and a renewed arms race.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages describing competition or rivalry among powers over AI as a security problem.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude corporate concentration concerns (AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION).
proposals.boundary_cases: If rivalry is only listed without link to security, code AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION alone.

examples.quote: Those challenges are aggravated by restrictive sanctions, trade wars, an intense rivalry in space, cybertechnology and artificial intelligence.

proposals.label: Battlefield AI challenging humanitarian law
proposals.definition: Use of AI on the battlefield is presented as challenging international humanitarian law, within a broader narrative of militarization and weaponization of new domains.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages stating that military or battlefield AI strains or violates international humanitarian law or is part of weaponization trends.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude weaponization of space or cyberspace passages that do not mention AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: A single-sentence mention of battlefield AI is still coded here because the military use is explicit, not as a generic list mention.

examples.quote: the use of artificial intelligence is challenging international humanitarian law on the battlefield

proposals.label: AI as concern of a privileged minority
proposals.definition: AI invoked as a topic of a fortunate minority, contrasted with global poverty and hunger to highlight inequality.
proposals.inclusion: Passages contrasting rich-world AI or technology debates with poverty, hunger or illiteracy elsewhere.
proposals.exclusion: Passages about unequal access to AI tools or capacity (still digital divide but with access framing).
proposals.boundary_cases: AI listed among rich-world concerns with no evaluation of AI itself should also be coded as a list mention.

examples.quote: while a fortunate minority in the world is discussing such issues as digital technology, robotics, artificial intelligence and obesity

proposals.label: AI listed among rich-world topics
proposals.definition: AI named in a list with digital technology, robotics and obesity without discussion of AI itself.
proposals.inclusion: Passages where AI is a list item illustrating a broader argument.
proposals.exclusion: Passages elaborating AI effects or governance.
proposals.boundary_cases: Code with AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE when the list serves an inequality contrast.

examples.quote: digital technology, robotics, artificial intelligence and obesity

proposals.label: Military AI deployed without agreed rules
proposals.definition: Concern that AI is being deployed for military use in the absence of agreed international rules, as part of a deteriorating security environment.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages noting military deployment of AI and the lack of rules governing it.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude civilian AI governance concerns and general nuclear proliferation without AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: Linking the gap to the Pact for the Future could also support AI_UN_ROLE if the Pact is cited as addressing AI.

examples.quote: Incredible new technologies like artificial intelligence are being deployed for military use without agreed rules.

proposals.label: AI benefits revealed by the pandemic
proposals.definition: AI and digital technologies presented as having helped during COVID-19, e.g., in medical diagnosis, and as opportunities for human development.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages crediting AI with health, education or development gains, especially in pandemic contexts.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages on AI regulation or threats.
proposals.boundary_cases: When AI appears only in a list of pandemic-era technologies, also code AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence has assisted doctors in making more accurate and timely diagnoses and finding the best treatment.

proposals.label: Balanced international AI regulation consensus
proposals.definition: Call to balance encouraging AI development with justified restrictions and build consensus on regulation averting military, technological and moral threats.
proposals.inclusion: Include calls for international consensus on AI regulation balancing development and restriction.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages only praising AI benefits.
proposals.boundary_cases: Mentions of military security threats within a regulation call may also get AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS.

examples.quote: seek for a right balance between encouraging the development of artificial intelligence and justifiable restrictions to limit it

proposals.label: AI listed among pandemic-era technologies
proposals.definition: AI named alongside IoT, cybersecurity and cloud computing as technologies offering opportunities, without further elaboration.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages listing AI among multiple technologies without AI-specific discussion.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages describing an AI-specific use.
proposals.boundary_cases: If the list is framed as development opportunity, AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS can be added.

examples.quote: the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, cloud computing and other applications

proposals.label: Technological power concentrated in few hands
proposals.definition: Concern that technological and AI power is concentrated among a few corporations and nations, raising questions of control and exclusion.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages naming concentration of AI or technological power in a few firms or states.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude access-gap arguments without reference to who holds power.
proposals.boundary_cases: When concentration is the premise for a governance call, also code AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: a world where technological power is concentrated in the hands of a few corporations and nations

proposals.label: Global governance for equitable, ethical AI
proposals.definition: Global governance must adapt so AI and new technologies are used equitably, ethically and for human well-being.
proposals.inclusion: Include calls for global governance to adapt to AI or ensure its equitable/ethical use.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude descriptive statements about AI transforming daily life without a governance call.
proposals.boundary_cases: Ethical-use language within a governance call is coded here rather than AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS unless rights are named.

examples.quote: Global governance must adapt to ensure that those technologies are used equitably, ethically and in the service of the well-being of humankind

proposals.label: Avoiding deeper inequalities and exclusion
proposals.definition: Warning that AI could deepen inequalities or create new forms of exclusion and control.
proposals.inclusion: Include warnings that AI will widen inequalities or exclude groups or countries.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude concentration claims without an inequality outcome.
proposals.boundary_cases: 'New forms of control' may overlap with surveillance concerns; code here when paired with inequality.

examples.quote: rather than deepening inequalities or generating new forms of exclusion and control

proposals.label: Generative AI superseding human skills
proposals.definition: Generative AI as progress that supersedes rather than optimizes human skills, with potentially tragic labour-market consequences.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages on AI replacing human skills or jobs and consequences for the labour market.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude productivity-gain framings without displacement concern.
proposals.boundary_cases: Displacement tied to wealth concentration is also coded AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.

examples.quote: progress no longer optimizes human skills but supersedes them, with potentially tragic consequences, especially for the labour market

proposals.label: Wealth concentrating at the top
proposals.definition: AI-driven change concentrating wealth among a few.
proposals.inclusion: Include claims that AI will concentrate wealth or power.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude between-country access gaps without concentration language.
proposals.boundary_cases: Brief concentration clauses in labour arguments are coded both themes.

examples.quote: with wealth becoming even more concentrated at the top

proposals.label: G7 push for balanced global AI governance
proposals.definition: Using a G7 presidency to help define global AI governance balancing innovation, rights, labour, IP, free expression and democracy.
proposals.inclusion: Include pledges to shape global AI governance through G7 or other forums.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude national regulation.
proposals.boundary_cases: Balance lists naming rights and democracy also support AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS.

examples.quote: defining a global governance for artificial intelligence that is able to strike a balance among innovation, rights, labour, intellectual property, freedom of expression and democracy

proposals.label: Questioning whether AI is intelligence
proposals.definition: Philosophical scepticism about calling data-processing systems 'intelligence', since intelligence entails asking questions.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages reflecting on the nature of machine intelligence versus human intelligence.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude ethics or rights claims that do not discuss what intelligence is.
proposals.boundary_cases: Claims that 'no algorithm can replace human conscience' are ethics (AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS) unless they define intelligence.

examples.quote: Intelligence entails asking questions, not answering them through data-processing.

proposals.label: Modern rules reconciling AI with ethics
proposals.definition: Call for states to build modern common rules reconciling AI development with ethical rules as part of digital transformation.
proposals.inclusion: Include calls for joint international rule-building on AI grounded in ethics.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages mentioning digital transformation without AI rules.
proposals.boundary_cases: The ethics component may also warrant AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS.

examples.quote: build modern rules that will allow us to reconcile the development of artificial intelligence with our ethical rules

proposals.label: Regulating big tech oligarchs
proposals.definition: Critique of a handful of tech oligarchs and big techs pursuing unregulated digital ultra-liberalism, bypassing the UN, and pressure from multinationals on national sovereignty.
proposals.inclusion: Passages calling to regulate big techs, criticising tech oligarchs, or resisting multinational pressure on digital infrastructure.
proposals.exclusion: General AI regulation calls without concentration critique (use AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
proposals.boundary_cases: Bypassing the UN Scientific Panel also takes AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: A handful of technical oligarchs want to resurrect a version of digital ultra liberalism without rules or transparency.
it would be an unforgivable historical omission not to address the challenge of regulating the big techs and artificial intelligence

proposals.label: Tech race bypassing UN scientific panel
proposals.definition: Concern that tech companies bypass the UN and its Scientific Panel on AI.
proposals.inclusion: Passages referencing the UN or the Scientific Panel on AI as bypassed or central.
proposals.exclusion: Passages without UN references.
proposals.boundary_cases: Combined with oligarch critique, code both.

examples.quote: bypassing the United Nations and the scientific panel on artificial intelligence

proposals.label: Protecting children and families from algorithms
proposals.definition: Companies shift algorithmic harms onto families; national legislation protects children, adolescents and women in the digital environment.
proposals.inclusion: Passages on protecting children/families from algorithmic or platform harms.
proposals.exclusion: General rights language (use AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS).
proposals.boundary_cases: Gambling platform harms count only when framed as algorithmic harm to families.

examples.quote: Companies that are aware of the risk of their products are transferring the impossible task of confronting algorithm to the families.
protect children, adolescents, and women in the digital environment

proposals.label: AI listed among technologies for partnership
proposals.definition: AI named in a list of cutting-edge technologies (Industry 4.0, nanotechnology, 5G) open for partnership, without further discussion.
proposals.inclusion: Passages listing AI among technologies for development or partnership.
proposals.exclusion: Passages elaborating AI risks or regulation.
proposals.boundary_cases: Conditioning partnership on sovereignty and data protection does not make it substantive AI discussion.

examples.quote: 4.0 Industry, artificial intelligence, nanotechnology and 5G technology

proposals.label: Strategic dependence threatening sovereignty
proposals.definition: Dependence on others in strategic sectors including AI is framed as a threat to the free exercise of sovereignty, requiring rethinking of value chains.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages treating reliance on foreign AI or digital supply chains as a sovereignty or strategic-autonomy risk.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general access-gap concerns without a dependence framing.
proposals.boundary_cases: When AI is one of several strategic sectors (health, food) in a dependence argument, still code here rather than AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION.

examples.quote: dependence on such strategic sectors as health, digital technology, artificial intelligence as well as food can call into question the free exercise of sovereignty

proposals.label: AI knowledge oligopoly concentration
proposals.definition: Concern about unprecedented concentration of AI in a few people, companies and countries, forming a knowledge oligopoly.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages about AI asymmetries, oligopoly, or concentration in few companies/countries.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude pure access requests without a concentration argument.
proposals.boundary_cases: Calls for AI 'with the face of the global South' fit here and in AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: we are experiencing the consolidation of asymmetries that could lead to a true knowledge oligopoly

proposals.label: Intergovernmental AI governance with all states
proposals.definition: Call for an intergovernmental AI governance system in which all states participate.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages demanding inclusive intergovernmental AI governance.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude multistakeholder or national-only governance.
proposals.boundary_cases: Emphasis on 'all States have a seat' also reflects AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE concerns.

examples.quote: We need a system of intergovernmental governance of artificial intelligence, in which all States have a seat.

proposals.label: Emancipatory AI respecting rights and data
proposals.definition: Vision of emancipatory AI that respects human rights, cultural diversity, personal data and information integrity, and serves peace not war.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages setting normative values for AI such as rights, data protection, cultural diversity, peace.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude concentration or governance-structure claims.
proposals.boundary_cases: 'Tool for peace, not war' is normative here unless military systems are discussed (AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS).

examples.quote: strengthens cultural diversity, respects human rights, protects personal data and promotes information integrity
Above all, it must be a tool for peace, not war.

proposals.label: Military AI, autonomy and nuclear escalation
proposals.definition: AI in the military domain: autonomous target selection and life-or-death decisions, the need for meaningful human control, and AI raising the risk of nuclear escalation.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages on AI used in conflict or weapons, human control over lethal decisions, or AI increasing nuclear/escalation risk.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude civilian AI safety concerns with no military or weapons context (AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL).
proposals.boundary_cases: AI listed with cyber capabilities as factors raising nuclear risk is coded here even if brief.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence has been used in conflict to select target and make decision over life or death.
the use of new emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, and the possibilities of cyberattacks, the risk of nuclear weapons use, either deliberately or by accident, is higher
the rapid development of artificial intelligences and cyber capabilities, increase the risk of escalation

proposals.label: Support for UN AI panel and dialogue
proposals.definition: Support for UN AI processes such as the Global Digital Compact, the independent international scientific panel on AI, and the Global Dialogue on AI Governance.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages naming or endorsing specific UN AI bodies or processes.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic references to multilateralism without a specific UN AI mechanism.
proposals.boundary_cases: Mentions of the Global Digital Compact without AI still count only if linked to AI or digital technology governance.

examples.quote: the establishment of an independent international science panel on AI and on the global dialogue on artificial intelligence governance are fundamental to promote scientific understanding of AI

proposals.label: AI's enormous opportunity and new risks
proposals.definition: AI is explicitly framed as offering enormous opportunity while creating new risks that must be governed.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages explicitly pairing AI opportunity with AI risk.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude risk-only military passages.
proposals.boundary_cases: If the passage moves from duality to a call for regulation, also code AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence and emerging technology offer enormous opportunity, but they also create new risks.

proposals.label: Rules must keep pace with innovation
proposals.definition: Calls to govern AI risks multilaterally, arguing no country can regulate global technology alone.
proposals.inclusion: Include calls to govern or regulate AI/technology through multilateral rules.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude UN-specific AI body endorsements without a general governance call (AI_UN_ROLE).
proposals.boundary_cases: Statements that technology must not undermine IHL can be coded here and AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS.

examples.quote: where new technology creates new risks, our responsibility is not to look away, but to govern them

proposals.label: Technology must not undermine rights
proposals.definition: AI and technology must serve humanity and not be used to undermine human rights or humanitarian law; human rights must be safeguarded in the digital age.
proposals.inclusion: Include statements that AI must respect human rights, ethics, or IHL.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude human rights content unrelated to technology.
proposals.boundary_cases: Meaningful human control over lethal AI decisions is coded AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS primarily.

examples.quote: It must not be used to undermine human rights. international peace or international humanitarian law.

proposals.label: AI incorporated into weapons systems
proposals.definition: Risks and threats from incorporating AI and emerging technologies into weapons and weapons systems, requiring international response.
proposals.inclusion: Passages on AI in weapons systems or new weapon technologies.
proposals.exclusion: Non-military AI risks.
proposals.boundary_cases: Criticism of arms sales counts only when linked to AI-enabled weapons.

examples.quote: the risks and threats posed by the incorporation of these new and emerging technologies into weapons and weapons systems

proposals.label: Societal benefits versus weapon risks
proposals.definition: AI recognised as having countless societal benefits while posing risks when weaponized.
proposals.inclusion: Passages pairing AI benefits with its risks.
proposals.exclusion: One-sided statements.
proposals.boundary_cases: If benefits are merely a preface to a weapons argument, code both.

examples.quote: artificial intelligence are progressing rapidly, with countless potential benefits to society

proposals.label: Filling the AI governance vacuum
proposals.definition: The absence of international governance on cyberspace and AI demands multilateral regulation and cooperation.
proposals.inclusion: Passages noting a governance vacuum for AI and calling for multilateral regulation.
proposals.exclusion: Misuse concerns without governance calls (use AI_CYBER_SECURITY).
proposals.boundary_cases: Calls for deliberation on preventing misuse also count here when framed as international cooperation.

examples.quote: The vacuum in international governance on cyberspace and artificial intelligence demands multilateral regulation.

proposals.label: Preventing misuse of dual-use AI
proposals.definition: AI's potential dual uses require deliberation on preventing misuse, without specifying military or criminal domains.
proposals.inclusion: Passages referencing AI's dual-use nature and preventing its misuse generally.
proposals.exclusion: Specific military use (use AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS) or cybercrime/terrorism (use AI_CYBER_SECURITY).
proposals.boundary_cases: If terrorism is linked explicitly to AI misuse, also code AI_CYBER_SECURITY; adjacent but separate terrorism statements do not qualify.

examples.quote: The potential dual uses of artificial intelligence call for urgent, informed deliberations on preventing its potential misuse

proposals.label: AI-driven disinformation undermining free speech
proposals.definition: AI used to mass-produce lies and convincing falsehoods, manipulate public debate and democratic processes, framed as a betrayal of freedom of expression.
proposals.inclusion: Passages on AI-driven disinformation, propaganda, manipulation of democratic processes, or deception at scale.
proposals.exclusion: Disinformation discussions that do not reference AI or automated tools.
proposals.boundary_cases: Online conspiracy theories without AI mention are context only; code when AI is named as enabler.

examples.quote: To distort free speech into the mass production of lies, propaganda, or AI-driven disinformation is not the exercise of freedom. It is its betrayal.
It is also making it easier to produce convincing falsehoods and manipulate public debate.

proposals.label: Faster international cooperation on AI
proposals.definition: Calls for governments, scientists and businesses to cooperate internationally, and quickly, to harness AI benefits while confronting risks.
proposals.inclusion: Passages urging international multi-stakeholder cooperation on AI.
proposals.exclusion: Passages only describing AI harms.
proposals.boundary_cases: 'Harness benefits while confronting risks' also signals duality; code governance when a cooperative call is made.

examples.quote: Governments, scientists, businesses must cooperate internationally to harness the benefits of AI while confronting its risks, and we need to move faster.

proposals.label: AI changing work and communication
proposals.definition: AI described as a transformation changing how people work, communicate and receive information.
proposals.inclusion: Passages describing AI's broad societal transformation of work and communication.
proposals.exclusion: Passages focusing solely on disinformation.
proposals.boundary_cases: If work is mentioned only as part of a broad transformation list, still code here briefly.

examples.quote: This revolution is changing how we work, communicate, and receive information.

proposals.label: Bots and AI misinformation lack free-speech rights
proposals.definition: Artificially generated misinformation and programmed bots spreading hate and lies are argued not to be protected by freedom of expression, which belongs to humans.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages on AI-generated misinformation, bots, propaganda or information integrity.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general human rights references to AI without information/speech content.
proposals.boundary_cases: Arguments about rights applying only to humans also touch AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS, but the disinformation focus is primary.

examples.quote: Freedom of expression is for human beings — not for programmed bots that spread hate, lies and fear
State-sponsored propaganda or artificially generated misinformation that is intended to sow discord and disunity

proposals.label: Multilateral cooperation against destructive AI
proposals.definition: AI raises serious questions demanding close multilateral cooperation to prevent it becoming a tool of destruction.
proposals.inclusion: Include calls for multilateral cooperation to manage AI risks.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages on AI benefits only.
proposals.boundary_cases: 'Destruction rather than creation' framing may also be read as AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY.

examples.quote: will demand close multilateral cooperation to avoid the very real risk of this technology becoming a tool of destruction rather than creation

proposals.label: Algorithmic isolation and manipulated content
proposals.definition: AI and platforms reinforce isolation via algorithms and enable manipulated images, alternative facts and disinformation that divide communities.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages linking AI or algorithms to disinformation, manipulated media, echo chambers or social division.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude cyber-crime or military concerns without an information dimension.
proposals.boundary_cases: Social-media-only criticisms without AI mention are excluded unless AI is named in the same argument.

examples.quote: The internet, social media platforms, and artificial intelligence offer us the illusion of connectivity
We are served alternative facts and manipulated images, making it easy to disseminate disinformation and sow seeds of division amongst communities.

proposals.label: AI listed among climate-adaptation sectors
proposals.definition: AI named as one sector in a list of areas where climate adaptation is embedded, without further discussion.
proposals.inclusion: Passages where AI appears as one list item among sectors (agriculture, energy, mining) in a climate or development narrative.
proposals.exclusion: Passages explaining how AI contributes to climate action or development.
proposals.boundary_cases: If the passage specifies an AI application for climate (e.g. forecasting), code AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS instead.

examples.quote: from agriculture and energy to infrastructure and livelihoods, to sustainable mining and artificial intelligence

proposals.label: Multilateral governance to mitigate AI risks
proposals.definition: Commitment to build multilateral AI governance to mitigate AI risks, aligned with the Global Digital Compact.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages pledging multilateral AI governance as a risk-mitigation measure.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude domestic digital regulation that does not address AI governance internationally.
proposals.boundary_cases: Explicit reference to the Global Digital Compact also fits AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: To mitigate the risks of artificial intelligence, we are committed to building multilateral governance in line with the global digital compact

proposals.label: Global Digital Compact as reference framework
proposals.definition: UN Global Digital Compact invoked as the framework for AI governance.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages anchoring AI governance in the GDC or other UN instruments.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude non-UN frameworks.
proposals.boundary_cases: Brief GDC mention inside a national digital-policy passage still counts.

examples.quote: in line with the global digital compact that was approved in this plenary last year

proposals.label: Domestic digital laws around AI
proposals.definition: National legislative measures in the digital sphere adjacent to AI: child online protection, digital market competition and sustainable data centres.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages describing national laws or bills on digital markets, data centres or online child protection presented alongside AI policy.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude national AI investment boasts without regulatory content (AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY).
proposals.boundary_cases: Child online-protection laws also fit AI_CHILD_PROTECTION if AI harms are explicit.

examples.quote: we sent draft bills to the National Congress to foster competition and digital markets and to encourage the installation of sustainable data centers

proposals.label: Military AI under international law, human control
proposals.definition: AI is discussed within arms control: control over military applications of new technologies, with AI developed under international law and effective human control.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages placing AI within arms control, military applications of new technologies, or human control requirements.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages about AI's civilian economic or social effects.
proposals.boundary_cases: A general 'international law' call for AI embedded in an arms-control paragraph is coded here rather than only AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: effective control over arms proliferation and the military applications of new technologies. Artificial intelligence must be developed in keeping with international law and under effective human control

proposals.label: AI as opportunity and risk
proposals.definition: AI briefly framed as both an opportunity and a source of risks, within a human rights context.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages explicitly stating AI is both opportunity and risk.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages that name AI only in a list without evaluative framing.
proposals.boundary_cases: Placement within a human rights paragraph suggests AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS only if rights impacts of AI are explicit.

examples.quote: New technologies, such as artificial intelligence, are an opportunity, but they also create risks.

proposals.label: Pact for the Future guiding balance
proposals.definition: UN outcome documents (Pact for the Future) cited as guiding a balanced approach to AI.
proposals.inclusion: Include references to UN pacts, compacts or processes as frameworks for AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general multilateralism with no AI link.
proposals.boundary_cases: If the Global Digital Compact is named, code here as well.

examples.quote: The Pact for the Future points the way to a virtuous balance in that area.

proposals.label: Common rules for AI before the strongest impose
proposals.definition: Calls for international rules, oversight and governance mechanisms for AI so technology does not operate in a rule-free zone or under the rules of the most powerful.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages calling for global governance mechanisms, common rules, or mutual oversight of AI/technology.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude calls for UN reform (e.g. Security Council) that do not concern technology.
proposals.boundary_cases: Passages framing the UN as the venue for AI rules may also be coded AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: This is precisely the task of the United Nations, to establish common rules before events or the strongest actors impose their own.
We need global governance mechanisms that ensure that such technologies respect ethical boundaries

proposals.label: Algorethics and human conscience over algorithms
proposals.definition: Ethical framing of AI: technology must serve humankind, respect ethical limits, and never replace human conscience or oversight.
proposals.inclusion: Include references to algorethics, human-centred technology, and warnings that algorithms cannot replace human conscience.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude purely institutional governance calls without ethical content.
proposals.boundary_cases: Moral arguments about technology 'capable of striking' lean toward AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS if weapons are the focus; code both when ethics is the frame.

examples.quote: We must guarantee the practical application of the concept of “algorethics”, that is, ethics for algorithms.
no algorithm can take the place of human conscience

proposals.label: AI control creating new domination
proposals.definition: Concern that those controlling AI gain enormous advantage, producing new inequalities, dependencies, concentrations of power or domination.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages warning of power concentration, dependence or domination arising from control of AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic inequality statements without reference to control of technology.
proposals.boundary_cases: Mentions of 'AI competition' among states without dependence or domination language go to AI_GEOPOLITICAL_COMPETITION.

examples.quote: Those who control these technologies will enjoy an enormous advantage over those who are left behind.

proposals.label: Govern AI without demonizing it
proposals.definition: Balanced framing that AI brings serious risks (job loss, manipulation, unsupervised decisions) yet unimaginable opportunities, so it should be governed rather than rejected.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages that explicitly weigh AI's risks against its benefits and reject both fear and unregulated adoption.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages mentioning only benefits or only risks.
proposals.boundary_cases: A long passage enumerating risks followed by benefits counts here, with specific risks also codable separately.

examples.quote: But governing innovation does not mean demonizing it.
Turning back is neither possible nor desirable, but neither can we hand over our future to technology without rules.

proposals.label: AI competition as front of global fragmentation
proposals.definition: AI rivalry among powers presented as one front of a broader breakdown of world order alongside wars, trade wars and hybrid attacks.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages naming AI competition or race between states as part of geopolitical fragmentation.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages on AI dependence of small states (AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION).

In fact, we must get ready for the new era, the unstoppable revolution. We need a responsible approach from all international institutions, the private sector, and also the governments. My country wants to contribute and to steer the debates and find solution by hosting all the actors at the Summit on Education and AI in Bratislava, in our capital, in November this year. Finally, at the UN's 80, I want to return to the matter of how to make it fit for the next decades. To be diplomatic yet frank, in recent years, it has not always been in the best condition to meet its tasks. Its credibility has been reducing. Yet it would be unfair and incorrect to say it is irrelevant or incapable. Over the past eight decades, the UN has provided us a space to speak on equal footing and to be listened to. Enemies can meet here eye to eye. It has succeeded in a wide range of areas. There have been groundbreaking agreements in many fields, including human rights, disarmament, climate, and health. G7, G20, BRICS, and other regional organizations, with their own goals, will never be able to fully substitute UN. However, the UN's health cannot be a justification for disengagement. On the contrary, the situation calls upon us for reinvestment in its strength. It lies in our hands, Member States, more than in the executive powers of the Secretary-General. UN reform is desirable and, in light of the current financial situation, also indispensable. Reform of the Security Council is long overdue, with representation of nations that better reflects the reality of the changed world. Slovakia welcomes the UN80 initiative.

This is the only way in which the two peoples can look forward to a decent life and a peaceful future. In the context of the developments in Iran, the security of global maritime routes, especially the route that passes through the Strait of Hormuz, have highlighted the global dimensions of this issue. As we underscored publicly several times in international fora, Bulgaria firmly supports the freedom and security of international maritime transport and calls for strict adherence with applicable international law and to the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. Security requires us to limit the risks posed by weapons of mass destruction and by their proliferation. Bulgaria remains determined to strengthen international nonproliferation, disarmament, and arms control architecture, as well as the three pillars of the Treaty on the Nonproliferation of Nuclear Weapons. We support the goal of a world without these weapons. which ought to be pursued via pragmatic measures, greater transparency, verifiable control, and limits placed upon arsenals. Global conflicts have introduced new threats hitherto unknown, jeopardizing nuclear safety through irresponsible attacks on nuclear sites. On the other hand, compliance with the Non-Proliferation Treaty is key for Iran, which ought first and foremost to adhere strictly to its international obligations and reach a long-term nuclear agreement overseen by the International Atomic Energy Agency. Today's security requires that we act in a timely fashion. This requires strengthening diplomacy, mediation, and political dialogue, as well as effective control over arms proliferation and the military applications of new technologies. Artificial intelligence must be developed in keeping with international law and under effective human control, and outer space must remain the realm of peaceful and safe operations. The same principle ought to guide our response to terrorism, radicalization, disinformation, and cyber threats. No country can do this alone. Ladies and gentlemen, strong institutions, effective UN peacekeeping operations, and closer international cooperation are necessary. Bulgaria will continue to defend this approach. Lasting security is not only built through responding to crises, but also through our capacity to prevent them, Excellencies.

We will continue to reduce redeforestation, which has been cut in half in the Amazon and reaching its lowest level in 11 years. We have the moral authority to reject protectionist measures disguised as commitment to the environmental cause. Brazil is a global reference in green energy. We have the critical minerals and the rare earths that the world needs to make the energy transition. Our natural wealth belongs to the Brazilian people and it is in their benefit that it will be exploited. Access to our minerals will be contingent upon mandatory value generation in our territory, technology transfer, and the supply of strategic national sectors. Mr. President, we are living through unprecedented technological revolution with great risks and opportunities. it would be an unforgivable historical omission not to address the challenge of regulating the big techs and artificial intelligence. A handful of technical oligarchs want to resurrect a version of digital ultra liberalism without rules or transparency. They are promoting a race with no ethical boundaries, bypassing the United Nations and the scientific panel on artificial intelligence. As Pope Leo XIV warned, decisions about technology should, quote, "should never be separated from awareness and responsibility," end of quote. Companies that are aware of the risk of their products are transferring the impossible task of confronting algorithm to the families. The billion dollar betting industry turns addiction into profit. Its exponential dissemination is increasing debt levels and destroying homes. Brazil will not tolerate this business model. We passed one of the most advanced pieces of legislations in the world to protect children, adolescents, and women in the digital environment. We will ensure fair compensation for artists, musicians, and other visual content creators. We will not give in to pressure from multinationals that want to privatize our PIX, a free public payment infrastructure that has made financial inclusion a reality for millions of residents. Ladies and gentlemen, the sustainable development goals are currently under attack from reactionary forces that wish to normalize injustices. Inequality and underdevelopment are the result of political choices.

More than 80 years ago, the Manhattan Project showed how rapidly a scientific breakthrough can transform the balance of power, and how difficult it is for politics and international rules to catch up. Artificial intelligence confronts us with a different technology and different risks, but with a similar lesson. Governance that comes only after the fact may come too late. If AI is to serve humanity, it must develop within a framework of international rules. No country and no company can meet this challenge alone. We need common standards, meaningful public oversight, and clear mechanisms of accountability. The choice is not between innovation and rules. It is between innovation governed by rules and innovation governed by the logic of the race. Ladies and gentlemen, artificial intelligence is not the only challenge that no country can manage alone. The same is true of climate change. This year has once again reminded us of the growing impacts of extreme weather, affecting people and communities across the globe. In many regions, Climate-related challenges are threatening homes and livelihoods. They are putting pressure on public health, food and water security, increasing living costs, and in some cases, contributing to instability and conflicts. The most vulnerable are often hit hardest. The Czech Republic has offered its support and stands with those working to rebuild their communities, but support after disaster is not enough. We need concerted global action, both to limit further damage and to adapt to changes that are already affecting our lives and will shape the lives of future generations. Mr. President, let me finish with a message that has not changed over the past year. Most of the challenges we face are global. No nation can meet them alone. That is why we need more dialogue, more cooperation, and more collective action. And that is why we must make multilateralism work. It is our common goal. Thank you.

But freedom that belongs only to people who fit someone else's definition of normal is not freedom. A society that strips people of their dignity will eventually undermine its own democracy. And nowhere is the backlash more extreme than in Afghanistan, where women and girls have been systematically erased from public life. Girls are denied education. Women are denied basic freedoms. For me, this can only be described as gender apartheid. On the Human Rights Council, Iceland, we have sought to match words with deeds, from Iran and Afghanistan to accountability for violations in Sudan. Throughout our Council term, Iceland will emphasize gender equality, LGBTQI+ rights, the rights of children and young people, and the relationship between human rights and the environment. Human rights are not for some, as we know, they are for all. Madam President, the same commitment to facts and responsibility must guide us on climate change. Leaders who deny or distort science should explain themselves to island communities watching the sea rise around them, to families losing land and livelihoods to drought and erosion, like in the Sahel. In Iceland, we can see the changes taking place in our own region, in the Arctic. Rising temperatures and receding ice are already changing ecosystems and the lives of communities across the region. Climate change is not an ideology. Millions already live with its consequences. We need to address it, not ignore it. Nor can we ignore another transformation already affecting our societies, artificial intelligence. This revolution is changing how we work, communicate, and receive information. It is also making it easier to produce convincing falsehoods and manipulate public debate. Freedom of speech is a fundamental right we must defend. But that does not require passivity when foreign states or other actors spread falsehoods, manipulate democratic processes, or use AI to deceive citizens at unprecedented speed and scale. Governments, scientists, businesses must cooperate internationally to harness the benefits of AI while confronting its risks, and we need to move faster. much faster.

Mr. President, last year, from this very podium, Italy's Prime Minister, Giorgia Meloni, recalled that 56 armed conflicts were raging across the world, the highest number since World War II. Today, those same sources put that figure at 61. It's the stark truth of the numbers. Pope Leo XIV issued a warning that Italy has made its own. We must never grow accustomed to war, because first we'll become accustomed to the words, then to images, and finally to the victims. When war becomes something we grow accustomed to, peace itself risks becoming a mirage. We will not give up. Against the law of the strongest, we choose the strength of the law. Against the politics of force, we choose the force of politics. This is the message Italy brings today to the United Nations. This is the mission of Italian diplomacy, to build bridges, open new paths, and keep dialogue alive, even when it seems impossible, to work for peace, prosperity, and growth, because growth creates prosperity, and prosperity in turn consolidates peace. Ukraine, the Middle East, the Gulf, Sudan, the Sahel are not separate crises, nor are trade wars, AI competition, hybrid attacks, and their economic and social repercussions, nor is terrorism in all of its many forms, which we continue to fight in every corner of the world. These are all different fronts of a single profound transformation. The world order that emerged after World War II is coming apart. It was an imperfect order. It did not prevent wars, injustice, or suffering. But today, the world balance has been disrupted, and history which someone has declared has reached its final chapter, is once again moving at a galloping pace. But every race needs a finish line. Our task cannot be to stand and watch passively the fragmentation of our world, but it must be to build a new framework of rules, responsibility, and cooperation capable of governing change.

To address this challenge, we are working side by side with United Nations Rome-based agencies, making available the best Italian expertise from agriculture and food production to satellite technologies that help reduce the use of land, water, and pesticides. Food security and water security are part of the same struggle. There can be no harvest without water. There can be no stability, only hunger, conflict, and migration if there is no water. Mr. President, dear colleagues, the choice between force and politics is not confined to war. It extends to the economy, resources, and technology. to every sphere in which unrestrained power risk prevailing over the human person. Politics thus must once again take the lead in shaping change. We stand at the dawn of a technological revolution that is already reshaping the way we live, the way we work, produce, and make decisions. It's the artificial intelligence revolution. The great inventions of the past took centuries to transform the world. Artificial intelligence is doing so in a matter of years. Those who control these technologies will enjoy an enormous advantage over those who are left behind. The risk is that new inequalities, new dependencies, and new concentrations of power, or even new forms of domination, will emerge. Entire professions may disappear or be transformed. Falsifying and manipulating reality will become ever more easier. Automated systems operating without human oversight may produce extremely dangerous decisions. Pope Leo XIV in the encyclical Magnifica Humanitas reminded us that no algorithm can take the place of human conscience and that any technology capable of striking without seeing the face of another person lowers the moral threshold for conflict. Italy shares this vision. But governing innovation does not mean demonizing it. Artificial intelligence can open up possibilities that today are unimaginable in medicine, for example, research, education, manufacturing, and environmental protection. Every major technological advance has generated fears, but has also created opportunities and over time, greater prosperity. Turning back is neither possible nor desirable, but neither can we hand over our future to technology without rules.

We do not need bureaucratic cages that can only be respected by some. We need a balance between transparency, oversight, security, and the protection of intellectual property. We need to share the benefits of innovation and build mechanisms of mutual oversight. This is precisely the task of the United Nations, to establish common rules before events or the strongest actors impose their own. The United Nations was founded in 1945 out of a world in ruins, a world that had learned a simple truth. When each of us stands alone, we all lose. 81 years later, that lesson is more relevant than ever. The United Nations was created to prevent violence from becoming the only law. But to remain faithful to that mission, it must regain its ability to make decisions and, above all, to act. With this conviction, Italy will continue to advocate for a universal moratorium on the death penalty, a cause rooted in civilization, in the defense of life and human dignity, which we have championed for years here in this very building. We are also on the front line in defending individual freedom and women's rights, and fighting, among other things, the abhorrent practice of female genital mutilation. We must have the courage to say it. Too often, this organization appears powerless. For far too long, its reform has been held back by competing interests. Italy wants a Security Council that is more legitimate, more representative, and more accountable to all member states. Not even a more exclusive club, but one of the pillars of the far-reaching renewal of the United Nations that we hope the new Secretary General will want to pursue, making it capable of deciding and acting while there is still time to change the course of events. Italy has always done its part and will continue to do so. We are among the leading contributors to the United Nations budget and among the top troop-contributing countries. We place men and women, our resources and our expertise at the service of peace in UNIFIL and in every mission in which we participate.

Until recently, Christian communities were a natural part of social life there. present for 2,000 years, helping to shape the culture, language, and identity of entire regions. Today, in many places, their numbers have dwindled dramatically. Sometimes, only traces of their former presence remain. Along with these people, a living tradition is disappearing: the heritage of the first centuries of Christianity. This legacy has been stopped in many places, and perhaps even lost. attacks on places of worship, discrimination, violence, and even loss of life. This is a reality that cannot go unanswered by the international community. Ladies and gentlemen, threats to human dignity no longer belong exclusively to the physical world. They are increasingly emerging in places where until recently, neither the law nor accountability extended in the digital realm shaped by the development of new technologies. New technologies, such as artificial intelligence or superintelligence, should always serve humanity as they develop, rather than exploit people or their weaknesses. This raises the question of whether, in a world of advancing artificial intelligence, humans will remain subjects or become merely objects of algorithmic influence. I am fully aware that groundbreaking technologies bring not only enormous opportunities, but also certain risks. As early as in the 1980s, an eminent Polish writer, Stanislaw Lem, in his novel "Fiasco" warned that the moment we teach machines to think, we will face questions not only about their capabilities, but also about their ambitions. Therefore, if they begin to imitate humans in their thinking, a natural consequence may be the drive to surpass them. Today, this challenge takes on a special dimension. It is precisely the development of technology that is playing a decisive role in co-shaping the realities of the 21st century. That is why we need a serious conversation about the limits of artificial intelligence development. We need rules that will actually be enforced and that clearly define where innovation ends and a threat to humanity begins. Artificial intelligence must not be used as a tool for destabilization, manipulation, or undermining the international order.

Technology must serve humanity and the truth, not chaos and manipulation. Ladies and gentlemen, Poland's priority is order based on truth, enshrined in our constitution and resulting from our historical experience. That is why we view the United Nations not merely as a forum for discussion, but as an institution that must be capable of taking action. The world is changing. The UN must change as well. We need an organization that can respond to violations of law, enforce principles, and prevent impunity. UN reform cannot be reduced to mere declarations. It must mean real effectiveness and accountability, including in the face of new challenges such as the demographic crisis or the development of artificial intelligence, which is outpacing existing rules and testing the limits of our responsibility. We are at a turning point. On the one hand, The logic of force and impunity is making a comeback. On the other, there are technologies that can either reinforce this logic or stop it. It depends on our decisions whether the law will prevail over force and whether humanity will remain more important than the tools it has created. Poland, and I want to convince you about that, ladies and gentlemen, will always stand on the side of the law, responsibility. humanity and freedom. Thank you.

San Marino called for the full restoration of the right of Afghan women and girls. Education is a right, work is a right, participation in public life is a right, dignity is a right. These rights do not disappear because a government choose to deny them. The international community must continue to stand with Afghan women and girls. Humanitarian access must also remain underrated. Afghanistan must not be forgotten. Mr. President, children everywhere deserve protection. Children are being killed, maimed, abducted, and recruited. They are losing their home, their school, and their future. San Marino remain firmly committed to the children and harm the conflict agenda and support the work of the UN Special Representative for children in harm and conflict. School must remain safe place. We have endorsed the safe school declaration, the Paris principle and the Vancouver principle. We call on all state to strain the protection of children in armed conflict and the ratify the optional protocol of the convention of the right of the child. Mr. President, the return of nuclear threat is another source of grave concern. There can be no acceptable nuclear threat or acceptable use of nuclear weapon. The modernization and expansion of nuclear arsenal, together with growing military expenditure and the rapid development of artificial intelligences and cyber capabilities, increase the risk of escalation. The consequences of nuclear use will be catastrophic. San Marino remain committed to a world free of nuclear weapons. We support the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons. We also proudly uphold the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, which San Marino has signed and ratified. Diplomacy must prevail over deterrence through fear. Peace and security cannot be separated from development. Nor can development be separated from human right. Conflict destroyed development gain. Poverty, food, instability. Climate change increased pressure on food, water, and community. We must also not overlook the devastating humanitarian and social and economic situation in Cuba. where prolonged hardship is placing an immense burden on the daily life of the Cuban people.

We must therefore treat peace, security, human rights, and sustainable development as part of the same agenda. The SDG remain our common commitment. The Pact for the Future provide an opportunity to strain multilateralism and accelerate implementation of the 2030 agenda. But commitments are not enough. We need implementation, financing, and accountability. We also need a fair and more inclusive international financial architecture supported by adequate resources and greater financial stability for the UN itself. The triple planetary crisis, climate change, biodiversity, loss and pollution is already affecting peace and security. Environmental degradation, food insecurity, water scarcity and displacement. The Paris Agreement must be fully implemented. The 1.5 degree goal must remain within reach. The transition must be just and no country should be left behind. Food security must also remain at the heart of our collective effort. Conflict and climate shock are driving hunger and malnutrition. San Marino believes that reducing food loss and waste is one practical contribution of a more secure and sustainable food system. We are also entering a new technological era. Artificial intelligence and emerging technology offer enormous opportunity, but they also create new risks. Technology must serve humanity. It must not be used to undermine human rights. international peace or international humanitarian law. The rule must keep peace with innovation. And where new technology creates new risks, our responsibility is not to look away, but to govern them. This is why multilateralism matters. Multilateralism is not an out-of-date idea. It is not only a framework capable of managing an independent world. No country can address today's challenge alone, protect itself from climate change alone, prevent the proliferation of nuclear weapons alone, or regulate global technology alone. And no country can build a lasting peace alone. We need cooperation and institutions that work. And we need the political courage to uphold the rule we have created together. Mr. President, for more than 17 centuries, San Marino has showed that a small state can preserve its independence through dialogue, respect for the law, and engagement with the international community.

Slovakia sees its engagement in UN reform as a part of its responsibility to this organization, including through UNAT and the implementation of the Pact for the Future. Our responsibility to the wider international order is also reflected in our candidacy for the Security Council for 2028 and 2029. We would be, of course, grateful for your trust and support. If elected, Slovakia will focus on four priorities: international law and the UN Charter, accountable security institutions, the protection of strategic resources and critical infrastructure, and the security challenges linked to digitalization and artificial intelligence. I fully share the concern of the United Nations about the inequalities that can be created by unequal access to artificial intelligence. It is in our common interest that innovation benefits all of humanity, not only the strongest economies or the biggest companies. If AI is available only to a few, new divisions will appear. Entire communities may be left behind. The growing use of AI-powered weapons and autonomous systems also requires urgent attention. One principle must remain clear: machines should never be allowed to make life-or-death decisions on their own. Just as the international community developed rules for nuclear, chemical, and biological weapons, We also need strong international frameworks for these new technologies. The United Nations can and should play a leading role in this effort. AI is not only a potential threat on the battlefield. It is already having a negative impact on society, especially in education. An entire generation of young people is being affected. Recent assessments show declining test scores across the vast majority of countries. This is a concerning trend that deserves open and serious discussion on international platforms such as the United Nations. At the same time, we should not see AI only as a risk. It can be also a tool for peace. It can help us analyze information, identify patterns, and overcome language barriers in real time. It can support better decisions, faster responses, and more effective prevention.

With responsible use, proper human oversight, and good governance, we can move this technology away from the battlefield and towards diplomacy, mediation, and conflict prevention. And prevention matters. Every conflict we prevent saves lives. It protects development. It preserves human dignity. Once violence begins, every solution becomes harder, more costly, and more painful. There is no need to reinvent the wheel when we reform international institutions. AI may be revolutionary. But we did not need to reinvent the personal computer in order to build it. The same is true in global politics. We should improve what already exists, not start again from zero. But let's ask ourselves a simple question. What if we, as world leaders, would start again following the UN Charter Would reform even matter if we finally did our best for global peace? Too many conflicts are still driven by the belief that political problems can be solved by force, by changing borders, violating sovereignty, and ignoring international rules. We need to reject this logic. Leadership is not shown by the willingness to escalate. It requires the courage to de-escalate. International rules may sound abstract in this hall, but on the ground, they are very real. They can mean the difference between life and death. When these rules are ignored, civilians suffer, communities are destroyed, millions are displaced, supply chains are disrupted, prosperity is lost. And there is even a deeper danger. If violence becomes normal for the next generation, diplomacy itself will become harder. What is difficult to solve today may become impossible tomorrow. That is why our most urgent task must be clear: stop the violence, keep diplomacy alive, and prevent today's conflicts from becoming tomorrow's normal. The war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year, continues to bring destruction close to Slovakia's borders. Attacks on civilian areas and critical infrastructure remain unacceptable. A ceasefire is still distant, and lasting peace even further away. We should support every serious diplomatic effort that can help end Russia's war against Ukraine and build a safe future for our neighbor.
